Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 50, verse 1:

Surah Qaf is Meccan [Al-Durr al-Manthur cites Ibn al-Daris, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Surah Qaf was revealed in Mecca." See al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/587.]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

﴿Qaf﴾ [Ibn 'Abbas said: it is an oath. And it was said:] [The words between the brackets are missing from manuscript "A".] it is the name of the surah, and it was said it is one of the names of the Qur'an.

Al-Qurazi [in manuscript "A" it reads al-Qurtubi, but the correct reading is what we have adopted] said: it is the key to His names "al-Qadir" (the Able), "al-Qadir" (the Powerful), "al-Qahir" (the Subduer), "al-Qarib" (the Near) and "al-Qabid" (the Restrainer).

'Ikrimah and al-Dahhak said: it is a mountain encircling the earth, made of green emerald; the greenness of the sky comes from it, the sky is propped upon it, and its two sides rest upon it [in manuscript "A" it reads "aknafuha", its sides]. It is also said that it lies beyond the barrier behind which the sun sets, at a distance of one year's journey. [Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (4/222): "It has been related from some of the early generations that they said: Qaf is a mountain surrounding the whole earth, called Mount Qaf. It seems that this, and Allah knows best, is among the fabrications of the Children of Israel, which some people took from them because of the permission to narrate from them what is neither confirmed nor denied. In my view, this and similar things are the inventions of some of their heretics, who used them to confuse people about their religion." See also: Al-Isra'iliyyat wal-Mawdu'at fi Kutub al-Tafsir by Shaykh Muhammad ibn Muhammad Abu Shahba (pp. 302–304).]

It was also said: its meaning is "the matter has been decided," or "what is to occur has been decided," as they said regarding Ha Mim [see above, p. 137].

﴿and the glorious Qur'an﴾ the noble and honoured one with Allah, abundant in good.

They differed concerning the answer to the oath. The people of Kufa said: its answer is "Nay, they marvelled" (bal 'ajibu). It was also said: its answer is omitted, its meaning being: "by the glorious Qur'an [added from manuscript "B"], you will certainly be resurrected." It was also said: its answer is His saying: "No word does he utter..." It was also said: "We have indeed known..." [See: al-Bayan fi Gharib I'rab al-Qur'an by Ibn al-Anbari: 2/384.]

The answers to oaths are seven: "inna" (indeed, emphatic), as in His saying: "And the dawn, indeed your Lord is ever watchful" [al-Fajr: 14]; "ma" of negation, as in His saying: "By the morning brightness, your Lord has not forsaken you nor has He detested [you]" (al-Duha: 1–3); the open "lam" (la-), as in His saying: "By your Lord, We will surely question them all" [al-Hijr: 92]; the light "in" (in), as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed we were in manifest error﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 38]; "la" (not), as in His saying: ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths that Allah will not resurrect those who die﴾ [al-Nahl: 38]; and "qad" (indeed), as in His saying: ﴿By the sun and its brightness — he has certainly succeeded who purifies it﴾ (al-Shams: 1–9).

"Bal" is used as in His saying: "By the glorious Qur'an, but they marvel" [50:1–2].

﴿That a warner has come to them﴾, one who warns and instils fear, ﴿from among themselves﴾, whom they know by his lineage, truthfulness and trustworthiness. ﴿So the disbelievers said, "This is a strange thing"﴾, something wondrous and bizarre.

﴿"When we have died and become dust?"﴾ we will be raised. The mention of the Resurrection is omitted because the context points to it. ﴿That is a return﴾, i.e., a restoration to life, ﴿far-fetched﴾ and impossible, i.e., it is far-fetched that we should be raised after death.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿We know what the earth diminishes of them﴾, i.e., what it consumes of their flesh, their blood and their bones. Nothing is hidden from His knowledge. Al-Suddi said: it refers to death, meaning: We know who among them dies and who remains. ﴿And with Us is a Book preserved﴾ [preserved from the devils and from being effaced or altered, and it is al-Lawh al-Mahfuz (the Preserved Tablet). It was also said: "preserving"], i.e., it preserves their number and their names.

﴿But they denied the truth﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿when it came to them, so they are in a confused matter﴾, mixed up. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: confused. Qatadah said regarding this verse: whoever abandons the truth, his affair becomes confused and his religion becomes unclear to him. Al-Hasan said: No people abandon the truth without their affair becoming confused. Al-Zajjaj explained the meaning of the confusion of their affair, saying: it is that they call the Prophet (ﷺ) at one time a poet, at another a sorcerer, and at another a teacher, and they call the Qur'an at one time sorcery, at another a rajaz (verse of a certain metre), and at another fabrication. Thus their affair was mixed and confused for them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 50, verses 12–17:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿The people of Noah, and the companions of ar-Rass, and Thamud, and 'Ad, and Pharaoh, and the brothers of Lot, and the companions of al-Aykah, and the people of Tubba'﴾. He is Tubba' al-Himyari, whose name was As'ad Abu Karib. Qatada said: "God, exalted is He, censured the people of Tubba' but did not censure him." We have mentioned his story in the commentary on Surah ad-Dukhan [[See above, pp. 233–235.]].

﴿Each one denied the messengers, so My warning was justified﴾, meaning: each of those mentioned denied the messengers, and My punishment became due for them. Then He sent down, as a reply to their saying, "That is a far-off return":

﴿Were We wearied by the first creation?﴾ That is: Were We incapable when We first created them, so that We became weary of resurrecting them? This is a rebuke to them, for they acknowledged the first creation and denied resurrection. It is said of anyone who is unable to do something: "'iya bihi" (he was unable to accomplish it).

﴿Nay, but they are in confusion﴾, that is, in doubt, ﴿about a new creation﴾, which is the Resurrection.

﴿And We have indeed created man, and We know what his self whispers to him﴾, meaning: what his heart speaks of, and his inner thoughts and hidden intentions are not hidden from Us. ﴿And We are nearer to him﴾, that is, more knowing of him, ﴿than the jugular vein﴾, because his parts and components screen one another, but nothing screens God's knowledge. "Jugular vein" (hablu al-warid) means the vein of the neck, which is a vein between the windpipe and the two esophageal passages (al-'ilbawain), spreading through the body. The "habl" is the "warid," so it is attributed to itself because the two terms differ.

﴿When the two receivers receive﴾, that is: the two angels assigned to the human being receive and take his deeds and utterances, preserving and recording them. ﴿One on the right and one on the left﴾, that is, one of them is on his right and the other on his left. The one on the right records the good deeds, and the one on the left records the bad deeds.

﴿Watchful﴾, that is: sitting. He did not say "two watchers" because he meant: on the right is a watcher and on the left is a watcher, so one was sufficient for the other. This is the view of the people of Basra. The people of Kufa said: he meant "qu'udan" (sitting), like "rasul" (messenger), which is used for both the dual and the plural, as God, exalted is He, said of the two: "So say: We are the messengers of the Lord of the worlds" [ash-Shu'ara': 16]. It was also said: by "qa'id" he meant the one who is constantly present and never departs, not the one sitting, which is the opposite of standing. Mujahid said: "al-qa'id" means "ar-rasid" (the watcher).

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 50, verses 38–40:**

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And We did create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no weariness touched Us.﴾ *Lughub* means exhaustion and fatigue.

It was revealed concerning the Jews, when they said: "O Muhammad, tell us what God created of creation in these six days." He said: "God created the earth on Sunday and Monday, the mountains on Tuesday, the cities, rivers and sustenance on Wednesday, and the heavens and the angels on Thursday until three hours of Friday. In the first of the three hours He created the causes of death, in the second the calamity, and in the third Adam." They said: "You have spoken truly, if you have completed it." He said: "And what is that?" They said: "Then He rested on Saturday and reclined upon the Throne." So God, exalted is He, revealed this verse in refutation of them. [[Recorded by al-Tabari (26/178–179) and al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul. See also al-Durr al-Manthur (7/609) and Ibn Kathir (4/230).]]

﴿So be patient over what they say﴾, regarding their lies, ﴿for God has an ambush for them﴾. This was before the command to fight them.

﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise﴾, that is: pray, praising God. ﴿Before the rising of the sun﴾, meaning the dawn prayer. ﴿And before its setting﴾, meaning the afternoon prayer. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Before its setting" refers to the noon and afternoon prayers.

﴿And during part of the night glorify Him﴾, meaning the evening and night prayers. Mujahid said: "And during part of the night" means the night prayer, at whatever time one prays.

﴿And after the prostrations﴾. The people of the Hijaz and Hamzah read *wa-idbara* (with a kasra on the hamza), as the verbal noun of *adbara*, *idbaran*. The others read it with a fath, *wa-adbara*, as the plural of *dubur*.

'Umar ibn al-Khattab, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i and al-Awza'i said: "After the prostrations" refers to the two rak'ahs after the sunset prayer, and "the setting of the stars" refers to the two rak'ahs before the dawn prayer. This is a narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn 'Abbas said: They said, "O Messenger of Allah, would that you frightened us," so this was revealed: ﴿So remind, by the Qur'an, whoever fears My warning﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 26/185. See also: al-Qurtubi: 17/28; al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/613.]]
